positive_findings: Exact source bytes and modes are checked against tracked HEAD before and after; symlink staging cannot masquerade as a published run.
Native HEAD must match configured revision and Godot4.6.3; CWD and explicit paths preserve the real Dart/Godot source boundaries.
Both owned process groups must terminate successfully;120s startup and1080s pair deadline; failures terminate only owned groups.
Original Dart/native outputs require matching legal seven-move history, final round/owner, token, exitACK, reward totals and same-process reopen.
Real geometry motion, one through seven discs and four winning markers must occur across actual successive PNG frames.
All nine current capture names and every original frame are decoded; the recording format is explicitly not deviceFPS.
v7 interface is compatible:170checks/248frames/ninePNGs and both process exits0; those local statistics are not substituted for a full published wrapper run.

findings.observation: The wrapper does not inspect original-godot.log for SCRIPT ERROR: or ERROR:. Godot can report an unhandled script error without a nonzero process exit; a separate unaffected test path could still produce passed:true.
findings.evidence_scope: read-only code-path finding; no extra reproduction executed
findings.suggested_change: Apply the existing strict native log-failure policy before acceptance, preserving ordinary WARNING lines such as unsupported VSync.

findings.observation: The final Dart/native owner values are compared to each other, but are not compared to the independently read initial session owner. A mode change legitimately changes roundId, so only owner and token should bind across that transition.
findings.suggested_change: Bind final owner/token to the captured handshake and require legal hexadecimal owner/round token syntax in the handshake.

limits: No new tests, Android execution, CI run, source edit or source/ref mutation by reviewer.
The existing15contracts and v4 decoder output were read, not repeated.
Current C4 v7 source is frozen separately; this review concerns only the proposed integration wrapper.
